5	 * For full license text, see the LICENSE file in the repo root or https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause
6	 */
7	
8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
12	 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
55	 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
56	 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
57	 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
58	 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
59	 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
60	 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
61	 *
62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 *
80	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
81	 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
82	 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
83	 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
84	 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
85	 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
86	 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
87	 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
88	 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
89	 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
90	 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
91	 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
92	 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
93	 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the
94	 * promotions engine, and whatever cart-item mapper eventually feeds this component real basket
95	 * data) is wired — neither is built yet as of this commit. Undefined (every existing caller today)
96	 * renders nothing — no empty node is emitted. See the prop's own JSDoc below for the styling —
97	 * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node): a real Figma
98	 * citation exists now (this paragraph used to say none did, true only in the sense that none had
99	 * been pulled yet), and the label renders via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"` rather than
100	 * the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
101	 *
102	 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
103	 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
104	 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
105	 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
106	 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
107	 *
108	 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
109	 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
110	 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
111	 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
112	 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
113	 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
114	 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
115	 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
116	 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
117	 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
118	 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
119	 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
120	 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
121	 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
122	 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
123	 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
124	 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
125	 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
126	 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
127	 * `message` prop above already establishes. Giving `ZimmInlineMessage` a real ARIA association
128	 * with this stepper is plan step 3.6, a later step not yet run as of this commit.
129	 */
130	import React from 'react';
131	
132	// Chakra Components
133	import {
134	  Box,
135	  Fade,
136	  Flex,
137	  Stack,
138	  Text,
139	  useMultiStyleConfig,
140	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
141	
142	// Project Components
143	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
144	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
145	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
146	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
147	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
148	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
149	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
150	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
151	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
152	import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';
153	
154	// Hooks
155	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
156	
157	// Utils
158	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
159	
160	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
161	
162	type SfccProduct = any;
163	
164	type ProductItemProps = {
165	  product: SfccProduct;
166	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
167	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
168	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
169	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
170	  /**
171	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
172	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
173	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
174	   */
175	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
176	  showLoading?: boolean;
177	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
178	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
179	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
180	  isRemoving?: boolean;
181	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
182	  /**
183	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
184	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
185	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
186	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
187	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
188	   */
189	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
190	  /**
191	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
192	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
193	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
194	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
195	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
196	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
197	   */
198	  message?: {
199	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
200	    text: string;
201	  };
202	  /**
203	   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
204	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
205	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
206	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
207	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
208	   *
209	   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
210	   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
211	   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
212	   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
213	   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
214	   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
215	   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
216	   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
217	   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
218	   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
219	   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
220	   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
221	   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
222	   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
223	   * `warning`).
224	   */
225	  discountLabel?: string;
226	};
227	
228	/**
229	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
230	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
231	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
232	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
233	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
234	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
235	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
236	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
237	 */
238	const ProductItem = ({
239	  product,
240	  primaryAction,
241	  secondaryActions,
242	  deliveryActions,
243	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
244	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
245	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
246	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
247	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
248	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
249	  showLoading = false,
250	  containerStyles = {},
251	  isRemoving = false,
252	  pickupInStore = false,
253	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
254	  message,
255	  discountLabel,
256	}: ProductItemProps) => {
257	  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
258	    product,
259	    false,
260	    false,
261	    pickupInStore,
262	  );
263	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
264	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
265	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
266	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
267	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
268	  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
269	  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
270	  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
271	  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
272	    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
273	      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
274	    );
275	  };
276	  return (
277	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
278	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
279	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
280	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
281	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
282	            <CartItemVariantImage />
283	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
284	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
285	                <Box sx={styles.itemInfoContainer}>
286	                  <Flex sx={styles.itemInfo}>
287	                    <CartItemVariantName />
288	                    <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
289	                  </Flex>
290	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
291	                </Box>
292	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
293	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
294	                )}
295	              </Flex>
296	
297	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
298	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
299	              )}
300	
301	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
302	                <Stack spacing={1}>
303	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
304	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
305	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
306	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
307	                    ) : (
308	                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
309	                        quantity={quantity}
310	                        min={1}
311	                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
312	                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
313	                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
314	                      />
315	                    ))}
316	                </Stack>
317	                <Stack>{!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}</Stack>
318	              </Flex>
319	
320	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
321	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
322	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
323	              {discountLabel && (
324	                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
325	              )}
326	
327	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
328	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
329	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
330	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
331	
332	              <Box>
333	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
334	                  <Fade in={true}>
335	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
336	                      {inventoryMessage}
337	                    </Text>
338	                  </Fade>
339	                )}
340	              </Box>
341	
342	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
343	            </Stack>
344	          </Flex>
345	
346	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
347	            <HideOnDesktop>
348	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
349	            </HideOnDesktop>
350	          )}
351	        </Stack>
352	      </ItemVariantProvider>
353	    </Box>
354	  );
355	};
356	
357	export default ProductItem;

/*
 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
 *
 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
 * component from a new component":
 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
 *
 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
 *
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
 * tested requirement.
 *
 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
 *
 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the
 * promotions engine, and whatever cart-item mapper eventually feeds this component real basket
 * data) is wired — neither is built yet as of this commit. Undefined (every existing caller today)
 * renders nothing — no empty node is emitted. See the prop's own JSDoc below for the styling —
 * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node): a real Figma
 * citation exists now (this paragraph used to say none did, true only in the sense that none had
 * been pulled yet), and the label renders via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"` rather than
 * the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
 *
 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
 *
 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
 * `message` prop above already establishes. Giving `ZimmInlineMessage` a real ARIA association
 * with this stepper is plan step 3.6, a later step not yet run as of this commit.
 */
import React from 'react';

// Chakra Components
import {
  Box,
  Fade,
  Flex,
  Stack,
  Text,
  useMultiStyleConfig,
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

// Project Components
import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';

// Hooks
import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';

// Utils
import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';

const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';

type SfccProduct = any;

type ProductItemProps = {
  product: SfccProduct;
  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
  /**
   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
   */
  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
  showLoading?: boolean;
  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
  isRemoving?: boolean;
  pickupInStore?: boolean;
  /**
   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
   */
  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
  /**
   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
   */
  message?: {
    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
    text: string;
  };
  /**
   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
   *
   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
   * `warning`).
   */
  discountLabel?: string;
};

/**
 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
 */
const ProductItem = ({
  product,
  primaryAction,
  secondaryActions,
  deliveryActions,
  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
  showLoading = false,
  containerStyles = {},
  isRemoving = false,
  pickupInStore = false,
  hideStepperAndActions = false,
  message,
  discountLabel,
}: ProductItemProps) => {
  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
    product,
    false,
    false,
    pickupInStore,
  );
  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
    );
  };
  return (
    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
            <CartItemVariantImage />
            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
                <Box sx={styles.itemInfoContainer}>
                  <Flex sx={styles.itemInfo}>
                    <CartItemVariantName />
                    <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
                  </Flex>
                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
                </Box>
                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                )}
              </Flex>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
              )}

              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                    ) : (
                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
                        quantity={quantity}
                        min={1}
                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                      />
                    ))}
                </Stack>
                <Stack>{!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}</Stack>
              </Flex>

              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
              {discountLabel && (
                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
              )}

              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}

              <Box>
                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                  <Fade in={true}>
                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                      {inventoryMessage}
                    </Text>
                  </Fade>
                )}
              </Box>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
            </Stack>
          </Flex>

          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
            <HideOnDesktop>
              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
            </HideOnDesktop>
          )}
        </Stack>
      </ItemVariantProvider>
    </Box>
  );
};

export default ProductItem;

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text, dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message' }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

13	 *     transitive dependency chain) unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`
14	 *     (`use-selected-store.js`), which throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a
15	 *     StoreLocatorProvider'` with no Provider present — round 2 rework fix, confirmed by reading
16	 *     that hook's source, not assumed. Nested inside MultiSiteProvider (its own body calls
17	 *     useMultiSite()), outside CommerceProviders (its one consumer, `useSelectedStore`'s internal
18	 *     `useStores` call, resolves with `enabled: false` here since no story sets a selected store
19	 *     in localStorage, so it never actually needs Commerce context — but this file nests it
20	 *     inside CommerceProviders anyway for a single consistent provider order). `config={{}}` is a
21	 *     deliberately empty stand-in — no story here drives real store-locator state, so there is no
22	 *     real config value to supply; PropTypes will warn on the missing required fields, which is
23	 *     inert noise, not a render failure.
24	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — item-attributes.tsx's usePromotions/
25	 *     useProducts/useProduct/useCurrentBasket (via
26	 *     `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket`). `disableAuthInit` +
27	 *     an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls; none of this story's mock line
28	 *     items carry priceAdjustments/bundledProductItems/type.bundle, so every one of those
29	 *     hooks resolves with `enabled: false` and never actually fetches.
30	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (item-price.tsx, product-item/index.tsx itself).
31	 *   ServerContext.Provider (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, not commerce-sdk-react) —
32	 *     found live in Storybook, not anticipated: item-attributes.tsx's useCurrentBasket() call
33	 *     above has its own separate transitive chain (useSFPayments -> useAppOrigin -> useOrigin)
34	 *     that calls the SDK's useServerContext() and destructures `res` from it unconditionally.
35	 *     With no Provider, useContext returns undefined and the destructure throws before useOrigin's
36	 *     own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res` at all) is reached.
37	 *     `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
38	 *     client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
39	 *
40	 * `GiftCard` story (round 2 rework): renders `ProductItem` with the new `hideStepperAndActions`
41	 * prop (SFCC-270 round 2, session-notes.md §11.2) set to true, on a plausible mock line item —
42	 * NOT a real gift-card detection, which this build still cannot do (see index.tsx's own docblock;
43	 * unchanged finding from the prior round). This story demonstrates the capability half only:
44	 * that when a caller explicitly asks to hide the stepper/actions, neither renders.
45	 */
46	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
47	import { fn } from 'storybook/test';
48	import React from 'react';
49	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
50	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
51	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
52	import { CurrencyProvider, MultiSiteProvider, StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
53	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
54	import ProductItem from '.';
55	
56	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	// Commerce provider stack (inert — no real API calls). See product-view/index.stories.tsx.
58	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
60	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
61	});
62	
63	const CommerceProviders = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
64	  <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
65	    <CommerceApiProvider
66	      clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
67	      organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
68	      shortCode="storybook"
69	      siteId="ZimmermannAU"
70	      locale="en-AU"
71	      currency="AUD"
72	      proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
73	      redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
74	      disableAuthInit
75	      silenceWarnings
76	    >
77	      <CurrencyProvider currency="AUD">{children}</CurrencyProvider>
78	    </CommerceApiProvider>
79	  </QueryClientProvider>
80	);
81	
82	const WithProviders = (Story: React.ComponentType) => (
83	  <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
84	    <MemoryRouter>
85	      <MultiSiteProvider site={{ id: 'ZimmermannAU' }} buildUrl={(path: string) => path}>
86	        <StoreLocatorProvider config={{}}>
87	          <CommerceProviders>
88	            <Story />
89	          </CommerceProviders>
90	        </StoreLocatorProvider>
91	      </MultiSiteProvider>
92	    </MemoryRouter>
93	  </ServerContext.Provider>
94	);
95	
96	// Data-URI SVG at the item-image `image` part's own ~2:3 ratio — no network needed, keeps
97	// stories deterministic in CI. Same precedent as zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx's own images.

101	});

103	// Shape matches getDisplayVariationValues's own real contract (product-utils.js): each
104	// variationAttributes entry's `values[].value` is matched against the sibling variationValues
105	// code, and its `.name` is what renders — "Lilac Sand" / "One Size" here, joined by
106	// CartItemVariantAttributes' own `combineAttributeValues` into "Lilac Sand, One Size".
107	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM = {
108	  itemId: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6',
109	  productId: '25595021M',
110	  id: '25595021M',

113	  price: 495,

125	  // Round 2 rework fix: useVariationAttributes' isVariantValueOrderable (base SFCC hook, called
126	  // unconditionally via useDerivedProduct) does `product.variants.filter(...)` with no guard —
127	  // an undefined `variants` throws. Empty array is enough: nothing in this story asserts
128	  // orderability, it only needs to not crash (confirmed by reading that hook's source).
129	  variants: [],

132	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM_TWO = {

name: vitest-coverage-report
          path: coverage/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Storybook interaction + a11y tests — runs on every PR to develop
  # and release/**. Exercises play() functions and @storybook/addon-a11y
  # component-level checks headless. Runs in parallel with unit-tests.
  # Runner: @storybook/test-runner (Playwright-based). Storybook is built
  # to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Cache Playwright browsers
        id: playwright-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            playwright-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        # playwright.config.js only ever configures Chromium-family devices (Desktop
        # Chrome, Pixel 5) — no WebKit/Firefox — so only that binary needs caching.
        # actions/cache can't reliably cache OS-level apt packages across ephemeral
        # runner images, so install-deps still runs unconditionally on a cache hit;
        # only the (slow) browser binary download itself is skipped.
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit }}" = "true" ]; then
            npx playwright install-deps chromium
          else
            npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
          fi

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

1	import React from 'react';
2	import type { Preview, Decorator } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
3	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { IntlProvider } from 'react-intl';
5	import theme from '../overrides/app/theme';
6	import { ZimmTokensGlobal } from '../overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal';
7	import { ZimmFontFace } from '../overrides/app/theme/fontFace';
8	import { CHAKRA_TOAST_A11Y_EXCLUDE } from './a11yExcludes';
9	
10	// @salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime's browser-side getConfig() (utils/ssr-config.client.js) just
11	// reads window.__CONFIG__, which the real app's SSR bootstrap script sets and Storybook never
12	// does — every call site that reads getConfig().app (Zimmermann's own, e.g.
13	// overrides/app/config/contentful.ts, and base SFCC vendor code, e.g. use-auth-modal.js's and
14	// otp-auth/index.jsx's getConfig().app.login) throws in Storybook without this. `login: {}` is
15	// needed alongside `app: {}` — every other getConfig().app.* read in base SFCC guards with `?.`
16	// or `|| {}`, but otp-auth/index.jsx's `const {tokenLength} = getConfig().app.login` does not,
17	// so `.login` itself must already be an object. `sites` is needed for any story whose play
18	// function clicks a button that calls useNavigation() → removeSiteLocaleFromPath() →
19	// getConfigMatcher() → getSites(), which throws when sites is empty. Not a copy of real config
20	// values — just enough shape for vendor code's unguarded reads.
21	if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
22	  (window as typeof window & { __CONFIG__?: { app: Record<string, unknown> } }).__CONFIG__ = {
23	    app: {
24	      login: {},
25	      sites: [
26	        {
27	          id: 'ZimmermannAU',
28	          alias: 'au',
29	          l10n: {supportedLocales: [{id: 'en-AU', alias: 'en-AU'}]},
30	        },
31	      ],
32	    },
33	  };
34	}
35	
36	// ZimmTokensGlobal injects the --zimm-* :root custom properties, mirroring what
37	// _app-config does in the app. Without it, the .zimm-* global classes and the
38	// var(--zimm-*) component overrides (button/header/listMenu) render unresolved in
39	// Storybook. Same shared source as the app, so the two cannot drift.
40	//
41	// ZimmFontFace declares the self-hosted Futura Round faces, likewise mirroring
42	// _app-config. Without it Storybook renders the fallback stack while the app renders
43	// Futura Round — the fallback measures ~13% wider, so any visual comparison made in
44	// Storybook would not match the app or Figma. Font files are served here by the
45	// staticDirs mapping in .storybook/main.js.
46	const withChakra: Decorator = (Story) => (
47	  <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>
48	    <ZimmFontFace />
49	    <ZimmTokensGlobal />
50	    <Story />
51	  </ChakraProvider>
52	);
53	
54	const withIntl: Decorator = (Story) => (
55	  <IntlProvider locale="en-AU" defaultLocale="en-AU">
56	    <Story />
57	  </IntlProvider>
58	);
59	
60	const preview: Preview = {
61	  parameters: {
62	    controls: {
63	      matchers: {
64	        color: /(background|color)$/i,
65	        date: /date$/i,
66	      },
67	    },
68	    layout: 'centered',
69	    a11y: {
70	      // 'error' causes a11y violations to fail test-storybook --ci runs
71	      test: 'error',
72	      // See a11yExcludes.ts — Storybook's parameters merge is shallow, so a story that sets
73	      // its own parameters.a11y.context.exclude REPLACES this array rather than extending it;
74	      // that file's own comment documents how a story adds to it instead.
75	      context: {
76	        exclude: CHAKRA_TOAST_A11Y_EXCLUDE,
77	      },
78	    },
79	  },
80	  decorators: [withChakra, withIntl],
81	};
82

1	/*
2	 * Copyright (c) 2021, salesforce.com, inc.

7	
8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotations and a
12	 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
13	 *
14	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
15	 *
16	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec. The outer Box's own literal
17	 * `width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100"` defaults are gone, replaced by item-variant.css.ts's
18	 * `image` part via `__css` — kept as `__css`, not `sx`, specifically so a caller-supplied
19	 * `width`/`mr` (e.g. order-summary/index.jsx's base, not-yet-overridden
20	 * `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />`) still wins; see that recipe's own docblock for
21	 * why. `{...props}` stays spread last, same defaults-then-spread order as before, still what
22	 * lets that caller-supplied width win. `ratio`'s default changed from `1` to the Figma-confirmed
23	 * 288/432 cart-item image ratio; the inner <Image> now also carries the `img` part's responsive
24	 * objectFit + mix-blend-multiply. Badge styling (Sale/Unavailable) is untouched — no Figma value
25	 * was given for it at this step.
26	 */
27	import React from 'react';
28	import {
29	  AspectRatio,
30	  Box,
31	  Badge,
32	  Image,
33	  useMultiStyleConfig,
34	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
35	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
36	import { FormattedMessage } from 'react-intl';
37	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
38	// Recipe key — single source in item-variant.css.ts (SFCC-270 round 2 rework), no longer
39	// redeclared per file.
40	import { ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE } from './item-variant.css';
41	
42	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
43	type SfccVariant = any;
44	
45	type ItemImageProps = {
46	  imageProps?: Record<string, any>;
47	  ratio?: number;
48	} & Record<string, any>;
49	
50	// Figma "Image" spec, product-item card (SFCC-270): aspect ratio 288/432, which reduces to 2/3
51	// exactly. Matches the design record's own 132x198 desktop pair exactly (132 * 432/288 = 198);
52	// against the 67x100 mobile pair it lands at 100.5 — half a pixel over the stated 100, the same
53	// class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's WIDTH_XLARGE note already documents for a
54	// different value, not something introduced here.
55	const CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO = 288 / 432;
56	
57	/**
58	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
59	 * main image.
60	 *
61	 * @todo = This component will render a `SALE` badge when the qualifier is available
62	 * on the custom property `c_isSale`. This will need to be expanded upon to handle
63	 * different badge/qualifiers and property names.
64	 */
65	const ItemImage = ({ imageProps, ratio = CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO, ...props }: ItemImageProps) => {
66	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
67	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE, {});
68	
69	  // We find the 'small' images in the variant's image groups based on variationValues and pick the first one
70	  const image = findImageGroupBy(variant?.imageGroups, {
71	    viewType: 'small',
72	    selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues,
73	  })?.images?.[0];
74	
75	  return (
76	    <Box __css={styles.image} {...props}>
77	      <AspectRatio ratio={ratio}>
78	        <Box position="relative">
79	          {variant.c_isSale && (
80	            <Badge
81	              position="absolute"
82	              top={0}
83	              left={0}
84	              marginLeft={2}
85	              marginTop={2}
86	              fontSize="10px"
87	              variant="solid"
88	              colorScheme="blue"
89	            >
90	              <FormattedMessage
91	                defaultMessage="Sale"
92	                id="item_image.label.sale"
93	                description="A sale badge placed on top of a product image"
94	              />
95	            </Badge>
96	          )}
97	          {variant.isProductUnavailable && (
98	            <Badge
99	              position="absolute"
100	              top={0}
101	              left={0}
102	              marginLeft={2}
103	              marginTop={2}
104	              fontSize="10px"
105	              variant="solid"
106	              colorScheme="red"
107	            >
108	              <FormattedMessage
109	                defaultMessage="Unavailable"
110	                id="item_image.label.unavailable"
111	                description="A unavailable badge placed on top of a product image"
112	              />
113	            </Badge>
114	          )}
115	
116	          {image && (
117	            <Image
118	              alt={image.alt}
119	              src={`${image.disBaseLink || image.link}`}
120	              ignoreFallback={true}
121	              __css={styles.img}
122	              {...imageProps}
123	            />
124	          )}
125	        </Box>
126	      </AspectRatio>
127	    </Box>
128	  );
129	};
130	
131	export default ItemImage;

/**
 * Generic right-anchored slide-in drawer shell — overlay, panel, and a Figma-matched size
 * variant (see ZimmDrawerSize), built on Chakra's Drawer primitive (focus trap, initial focus,
 * focus restore, body-scroll lock, and Escape/overlay-click-to-close all come from Chakra, not
 * hand-rolled).
 *
 * Pass `title` to render an inline header row (title text left, close button right) sized per the
 * Figma drawer/header frames. Omit `title` and pass `labelledBy`/`aria-label` instead for drawers
 * that supply their own header (e.g. ZimmPdpDrawer's tab row), which keeps the floating close
 * button behaviour.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmDrawerProps
 */
export const ZimmDrawer = (props: ZimmDrawerProps) => {
  const { isOpen, onClose, size, children, titleStyle = 'large', finalFocusRef, initialFocusRef } = props;
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_DRAWER_RECIPE, { variant: size });
  const titleId = useId();

  // Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: without an explicit `initialFocusRef`, Chakra's Drawer
  // defaults to auto-focusing the first focusable descendant — for every real consumer that
  // doesn't set one (ZimmCartDrawer, ZimmPdpDrawer), that's the close button. Reproduced live:
  // when nothing has focus and no prior user interaction exists yet (confirmed exactly matching
  // how a Storybook story that mounts already-open behaves, and plausible for a real first
  // render too), the browser's native `:focus-visible` heuristic has no basis to rule out a
  // keyboard interaction and defaults to showing the ring — on the close button, on every open,
  // regardless of whether the shopper used a mouse, touch, or keyboard to get there. `panelRef`
  // gives Chakra a neutral target instead: the dialog's own panel, `tabIndex={-1}` so it's
  // programmatically focusable without joining the normal Tab order. This still satisfies the
  // real requirement (focus moves into the dialog immediately, so keyboard/AT users land
  // somewhere sane and Tab/Escape work correctly from there) without ever auto-focusing an
  // interactive element nobody actually interacted with. A consumer that explicitly passes its
  // own `initialFocusRef` (ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer, straight to its email field) is untouched —
  // this only changes the *default* Chakra would otherwise have picked.
  const panelRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const title = 'title' in props ? props.title : undefined;
  const labelledBy = !title && 'labelledBy' in props ? props.labelledBy : undefined;
  const ariaLabel = !title && 'aria-label' in props ? props['aria-label'] : undefined;

  // SFCC-926 — tester reported body scroll still active while any drawer is open, allowing
  // the page behind the overlay to scroll alongside the drawer. ZimmDrawer bypasses Chakra's
  // own <DrawerContent>, so blockScrollOnMount may not fire. Locking body overflow explicitly
  // ensures only the drawer's internal scroll area is accessible while it is open.
  // Uses the module-level counter so multiple open instances don't race to restore overflow.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) return;
    if (scrollLockCount === 0) {
      scrollLockPrev = document.body.style.overflow;
      document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
    }
    scrollLockCount++;
    return () => {
      scrollLockCount--;
      if (scrollLockCount === 0) {
        document.body.style.overflow = scrollLockPrev;
        scrollLockPrev = '';
      }
    };
  }, [isOpen]);

  // Chakra's FocusLock remains active during the exit animation, so any focus call made
  // while the drawer is still mounted (rAF, close-button onClick) gets trapped and dropped.
  // onCloseComplete fires after the animation finishes and FocusLock is released — the only
  // reliable moment to restore focus. Covers both close-button click and Escape for all
  // consumers that pass finalFocusRef.
  const handleCloseComplete = () => {
    if (finalFocusRef) finalFocusRef.current?.focus();
  };

 *     ("Item Info | flex-col, name above price | flex-row justify-between") was never carried
 *     into `plan.md`'s actual step 2.2 scope — closed here, 2026-09-19, not part of the
 *     original SFCC-270 restyle.

 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/

        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop

        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
        alignItems: 'flex-start',

1	/**
2	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
3	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
4	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
5	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
6	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
7	 * type/colour/icon.)
8	 *
9	 * Two-part multipart recipe (`root`/`text`), following zimmDrawer.css.ts's plain-object
10	 * `{parts, baseStyle, variants}` shape rather than `defineStyleConfig` — no Chakra helper
11	 * factory, same Chakra-native string `variants` resolution either form supports.
12	 *
13	 * Restructured from a single-node `defineStyleConfig` (SFCC-795 rework — Marcel's own visual
14	 * checkpoint against the real Figma file surfaced a genuine gap the original single-node shape
15	 * couldn't express): the `warning` variant carries a leading 16x16 icon, the `error` variant
16	 * never does. This was already a known requirement, not something discovered fresh at the
17	 * checkpoint or borrowed from an unrelated ticket — `.claude/session-notes.md:395` (the original
18	 * SFCC-795 ticket restatement, written before any Figma metadata was pulled) already says
19	 * "warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. 'Maximum purchase quantity reached for this
20	 * size')", the exact copy string used here. It was simply dropped somewhere between that
21	 * restatement and the written build plan's step 3.2 text, and the checkpoint is what caught it.
22	 *
23	 * Confirmed against 3 real cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs
24	 * ("Zimmermann_Designs") — the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS
25	 * node 9323-98397) have a bare `<text>` message sub-tree, no icon; the warning-copy state's own
26	 * "Cart Item" instance is `icon(16x16, x=0) -> 8px gap -> text(x=24)`. That instance is node
27	 * 9323:106685, named "Cart Item" — confirmed via its own metadata to be one of 5 per-item rows
28	 * inside the "Cart-item-group" frame, i.e. genuinely SFCC-270/795's own per-item scope. It is
29	 * NOT the same as "Cart-level-messages" (a distinct sibling instance, 1186x52, that the same
30	 * top-level "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame (9323-90299) also contains at the page level) — that one is
31	 * SFCC-404's cart-level banner, a wholly different component this build does not touch. The two
32	 * share a parent frame and a similar 8px gap value, which is what makes them easy to conflate at
33	 * a glance; the "Cart Item"/"Cart-level-messages" instance names are what actually disambiguate
34	 * them, confirmed directly rather than inferred from proximity.
35	 *
36	 * So the single implicit node this recipe used to describe is no longer enough: `root` is now
37	 * the flex row wrapping the optional icon + the text, and `text` carries what used to be the
38	 * whole recipe's `baseStyle`.
39	 *
40	 * No separate `icon` part: `ZimmIcon`'s own `color` prop defaults to `currentColor`
41	 * (zimmIcon/index.tsx), and Chakra's `Icon` component passes `color` straight through as the
42	 * rendered SVG's own inline CSS `color` rather than resolving it to a token itself (confirmed
43	 * directly in `@chakra-ui/icon`'s `Icon` implementation) — so the icon element's own
44	 * `stroke="currentColor"` shapes (zimm.tsx's `InfoSolidIcon`) inherit `root`'s `color` via
45	 * ordinary CSS inheritance for free. Nothing to declare on this recipe's side for the icon.
46	 *
47	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
48	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
49	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
50	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
51	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
52	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
53	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
54	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
55	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
56	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
57	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below, on the `text` part, to override the
58	 * textStyle-expanded medium value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied
59	 * after the textStyle expansion wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's
60	 * `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already documents and relies on for the identical reason.
61	 *
62	 * `root.width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly,
63	 * rather than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default — moved here
64	 * from the (no-longer-existing) single node, since `root` is now the outer container.
65	 *
66	 * `root.alignItems: 'flex-start'`: top-aligned, not centred — the warning icon sits at the top
67	 * of what can be 2-line-wrapped text, not vertically centred against it. Confirmed via the
68	 * Figma metadata's own y-positions on the "Cart Item" instance cited above (9323:106685): the
69	 * icon instance sits at y=0 within its frame, the same top edge the text frame starts from.
70	 *
71	 * `root.gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'` (8px): that same "Cart Item" instance places the 16px-wide icon at
72	 * x=0 and the text frame starting at x=24 — the 8px difference between them is the gap.
73	 *
74	 * Three variants, not two — corrected SFCC-795 plan step 3.3, 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma

93	    width: 'full',

98	    // Standard flexbox text-truncation-prevention: without these, a long message next to the
