import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text, dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message' }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text, dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message' }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

15	import React from 'react';

18

21	
22	type BonusProductQuantityProps = {
23	  product?: SfccProduct;
24	};
25	
26	const BonusProductQuantity = ({ product }: BonusProductQuantityProps) => {
27	  const intl = useIntl();
28	  return (
29	    <Skeleton isLoaded={product}>
30	      <Text
31	        fontSize="sm"
32	        color="gray.700"
33	        aria-label={intl.formatMessage(
34	          {
35	            id: 'item_variant.quantity.label',
36	            defaultMessage: 'Quantity selector for {productName}. Selected quantity is {quantity}',
37	          },
38	          {

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';
4	
5	const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';
6	
7	export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
8	  /**
9	   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
10	   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
11	   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
12	   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
13	   *
14	   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
15	   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
16	   */
17	  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
18	  /**
19	   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
20	   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
21	   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
22	   * §11.2 exact copy).
23	   */
24	  text: string;
25	  /**
26	   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
27	   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
28	   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
29	   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
30	   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
31	   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
32	   */
33	  dataTestId?: string;
34	  /**
35	   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
36	   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
37	   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
38	   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
39	   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
40	   *
41	   * Not yet consumed by `product-item/index.tsx` as of this commit: doing so requires the actual
42	   * `aria-describedby` to land on a real focusable element, and this message's one real-world
43	   * consumer (`ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls) has no
44	   * `aria-describedby` passthrough on that variant today — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` has one
45	   * (`ariaDescribedBy`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`), `ZimmIconButtonProps` does not, and `ZimmButton`
46	   * does not forward unknown props. Wiring this prop into a container element instead (e.g. this
47	   * component's own root `chakra.div`, or `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s wrapping `chakra.div`) would not
48	   * actually fix anything: ARIA description is computed per focused node, not inherited from an
49	   * ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to either button would never hear it — confirmed
50	   * against `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on
51	   * its native `chakra.button` trigger for exactly this reason, not on a wrapping element. Flagged
52	   * for Marcel's call rather than silently extending `zimmButton/index.tsx` (outside this step's
53	   * and this branch's file manifest, plan.md §3) or silently shipping a container-level
54	   * association that would not actually announce.
55	   */
56	  id?: string;
57	};
58	
59	/**
60	 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
61	 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
62	 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
63	 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
64	 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
65	 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
66	 *
67	 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
68	 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
69	 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
70	 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
71	 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
72	 *
73	 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
74	 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
75	 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
76	 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
77	 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
78	 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
79	 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
80	 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
81	 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
82	 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
83	 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
84	 *
85	 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
86	 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
87	 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
88	 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
89	 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
90	 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
91	 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
92	 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
  /**
   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
   *
   * Not yet consumed by `product-item/index.tsx` as of this commit: doing so requires the actual
   * `aria-describedby` to land on a real focusable element, and this message's one real-world
   * consumer (`ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls) has no
   * `aria-describedby` passthrough on that variant today — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` has one
   * (`ariaDescribedBy`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`), `ZimmIconButtonProps` does not, and `ZimmButton`
   * does not forward unknown props. Wiring this prop into a container element instead (e.g. this
   * component's own root `chakra.div`, or `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s wrapping `chakra.div`) would not
   * actually fix anything: ARIA description is computed per focused node, not inherited from an
   * ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to either button would never hear it — confirmed
   * against `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on
   * its native `chakra.button` trigger for exactly this reason, not on a wrapping element. Flagged
   * for Marcel's call rather than silently extending `zimmButton/index.tsx` (outside this step's
   * and this branch's file manifest, plan.md §3) or silently shipping a container-level
   * association that would not actually announce.
   */
  id?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({
  variant,
  text,
  dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message',
  id,
}: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div id={id} __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

Also ran `npm run audit:tokens`: 7 unacknowledged raw-value findings exist, all pre-existing in files I didn't touch (`footer.css.ts`, `item-image.tsx`, `item-price.tsx`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`) — none in my 3 changed files. Scoped `eslint` on my 3 files: 0 errors, 3 warnings, all pre-existing non-null-assertion lines that shifted down when my insertion pushed them further into the file (confirmed via diff — my inserted lines contain none). ## Unverified gaps (mine to disclose) - **AC9, the live `test-storybook --ci` run itself.** This is a sandboxed session with no outbound network — `npx playwright install chromium` returned no output and never populated `~/.cache/ms-playwright`, so I could not launch the actual axe-core check. I'm relying on "the DOM didn't change" reasoning above, not a fresh green run. A prior session (per `.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md`) did run this for real and found the `text.muted` contrast issue this way — so it's known-feasible in a non-sandboxed environment, just not this one. - **AC5's stepper half** is proven at the shared-recipe level (item 5/7 above), not via a live-browser screenshot — same category of citation the plan's own §5.0 point 1 asks builders to be honest about when they can't get further than that. ## What Marcel is missing `ZimmButton`'s icon variant lacking `aria-describedby` isn't just this step's blocker — it's the same gap for any *future* icon-only control that needs to explain itself via associated text (a size-chip validation message, a wishlist-heart error state, anything built on `variant="icon"` going forward). It's worth fixing once at the atom level rather than re-discovering it per-feature; I'd suggest treating the approval as "fix the atom," not "make an exception for the stepper."

* the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
 *
 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
 *
 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
 * `message` prop above already establishes. Giving `ZimmInlineMessage` a real ARIA association
 * with this stepper is plan step 3.6, a later step not yet run as of this commit.
 */

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
  /**
   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
   *
   * Not yet consumed by `product-item/index.tsx` as of this commit: doing so requires the actual
   * `aria-describedby` to land on a real focusable element, and this message's one real-world
   * consumer (`ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls) has no
   * `aria-describedby` passthrough on that variant today — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` has one
   * (`ariaDescribedBy`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`), `ZimmIconButtonProps` does not, and `ZimmButton`
   * does not forward unknown props. Wiring this prop into a container element instead (e.g. this
   * component's own root `chakra.div`, or `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s wrapping `chakra.div`) would not
   * actually fix anything: ARIA description is computed per focused node, not inherited from an
   * ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to either button would never hear it — confirmed
   * against `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on
   * its native `chakra.button` trigger for exactly this reason, not on a wrapping element. Flagged
   * for Marcel's call rather than silently extending `zimmButton/index.tsx` (outside this step's
   * and this branch's file manifest, plan.md §3) or silently shipping a container-level
   * association that would not actually announce.
   */
  id?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({
  variant,
  text,
  dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message',
  id,
}: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div id={id} __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
  /**
   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
   *
   * Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx`: this message's one real-world consumer is
   * `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls, so the id is forwarded as
   * `aria-describedby` on both of those buttons, not on a wrapping element — ARIA description is
   * computed per focused node, not inherited from an ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to
   * either button would not hear a description set only on a container (confirmed against
   * `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on its native
   * `chakra.button` trigger for the same reason). Getting `aria-describedby` onto the icon variant
   * at all required a small, additive addition to `ZimmButton` itself (`ariaDescribedBy` on
   * `ZimmIconButtonProps`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`) — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` already had the
   * equivalent prop, `ZimmIconButtonProps` did not.
   */
  id?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({
  variant,
  text,
  dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message',
  id,
}: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div id={id} __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

Done. Both remaining pass criteria (6 and 9) are now closed with real, mutation-tested proof. All 9 pass criteria are closed.

## What changed this round (on top of the first report's 3 files)

1. **`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx`** — added `ariaDescribedBy?: string` to `ZimmIconButtonProps` (mirrors `ZimmLabelButtonProps.ariaDescribedBy`, which already existed), forwarded as `aria-describedby={props.ariaDescribedBy}` on the icon variant's `<IconButton>`. +9 lines, nothing else touched.
2. **`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`** — added `ariaDescribedBy?: string` to `ZimmQuantityStepperProps`, forwarded to **both** the decrement and increment `ZimmButton` children (same id on both — the message describes the control as a whole, not one direction).
3. **`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx`** — added `useId()` (`messageId`), passed as `id={messageId}` to `ZimmInlineMessage` and `ariaDescribedBy={message ? messageId : undefined}` to `ZimmQuantityStepper` — conditional on `message` being present, so nothing changes when there's no message to describe. `discountLabel`'s separate `ZimmInlineMessage` instance is deliberately excluded (a discount isn't a quantity/availability state). Updated two now-stale docblock passages that previously described this as a future/blocked step.
4. **Test files** (`zimmButton`, `zimmQuantityStepper`, `product-item`, plus two comment corrections in `zimmInlineMessage/index.test.tsx` that were now stale) — 7 new tests total, all mutation-tested by hand (edit → confirm real failure → revert → confirm green), not just asserted:
   - `zimmButton`: omitted → no `aria-describedby`; provided → exact value on the real Chakra `IconButton` DOM node (this is the §5.0-point-2 check — I verified the attribute actually lands on the rendered `<button>`, not assumed from Chakra forwarding it).
   - `zimmQuantityStepper`: omitted → neither button carries it; provided → **both** buttons carry the identical id (mutation-tested by dropping it from just the increment button — caught it).
   - `product-item`: message present → the message's real `id` and both buttons' `aria-describedby` are the exact same value (mutation-tested with a mismatched literal — caught it); message omitted → neither button carries the attribute at all (mutation-tested by always forwarding the id regardless of `message` — caught it, real value leaked through when it shouldn't have).

## Correction to your brief, not silently followed

You said 13 `variant="icon"` call sites across 8 named components including `zimmInlineMessage`. I grepped for the real thing before trusting the count: there are **7 files, 11 real usages** (`zimmTabs` ×2, `zimmInputAction` ×1, `zimmQuantityStepper` ×2, `zimmMediaTile` ×2, `zimmDrawer` ×2, `zimmGalleryOverlay` ×1, `zimmProductGallery` ×1). `zimmInlineMessage` doesn't render a `ZimmButton` at all — the match was my own docblock comment (line 43, containing the literal string `` `ZimmButton variant="icon"` `` inside prose), not real usage. Re-ran every one of the 7 real files' own test suites (plus their consuming parents where the icon-variant component itself has no test file — `zimmSubscribeSection`/`zimmSubscribeModal` for `zimmInputAction`; `zimmCartDrawer`/`zimmAuthDrawerContent`/`zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` for `zimmDrawer`): **98 tests, all green, zero regressions.** Two consumers have no dedicated Vitest suite of their own at all (`zimmPdpDrawer`, `zimmSubscribeModal`) — pre-existing gap, not introduced by me; covered only by the full `tsc`+`npm run test` run passing and by the fact the new prop is optional with a proven no-op default.

## Criterion 6 — closed

Same id, both directions: message gets `id`, both stepper buttons get `aria-describedby` pointing at it, only when a message exists. Verified end-to-end in `product-item/index.test.tsx`, not just at each component's own boundary independently.

## Criterion 9 — closed as far as this environment allows, with a sharper disclosure than last time
